class: Any product rule an orchestrator writes into a builder brief from memory or paraphrase, instead of quoting the spec text it rests on, can be wrong, and the builder then implements the wrong rule faithfully and its tests lock it in, costing a full fix round when a verifier catches it.
mechanism: The brief states the rule as settled; the builder has no reason to doubt it; the spec's actual words (or the owner-reviewed source) say something else.

first_seen.where: night build, orchestrator briefs for W-001, W-015, W-014, W-004
first_seen.evidence: W-001 brief: 'UNLIMITED when the tail slope is non-zero in that direction' (wrong: an index can't go below 0; builder flagged it). W-015 brief invented a key-name secret guard no AC defines (two failed rounds). W-014 brief rule (b) entry-price worst case blocked hedged partial exits (builder flagged it). W-004 brief: header 'NIFTY at expiry | You make/lose' on every Guided column, while the owner-reviewed T1 table uses it as a pair of headings (verifier failed AC-7; item parked). Also caught before harm: 'Near adjustment' instead of ADR-010's 'Adjustment opportunity'.

occurrences.evidence: independent review: no AC defines it
builder measurement -14,170 -> -19,825 on a hedged close
'Near adjustment' vs ADR-010 'Adjustment opportunity', corrected before the build

brief said a 'max loss 5,000' rule fires on the golden Iron Condor; at the golden LTPs the condor is +1,365 in profit, so no max-loss rule can fire (W-020 builder flagged it and built a separate loss scenario, hand-computed -3,450.00)

brief said 'refuse the call if there is no active version'; ADR-009 Q17 / REQ-041 entry conditions and ADR-019 Q202 'entry triggered' fire before any execution, so the refusal dropped a spec-required record; builder applied it, orchestrator caught it on reading the side-effect note and reversed it (7717c98)

brief said 'include the exact current level as the first value, then 100-point multiples away from it'; built as offsets from an unaligned level, so SENSEX 81,422 gave 81,322 (not a strike) and the REQ-026 note 'every value is a real strike' became false; verifier failed AC-5

brief named only AFTER_EXECUTION and ORDER_EVENT for account-wide coverage; the PERIODIC trigger still compared active ids only, so a Monitoring Paused holder of a shared contract caused a false block and a corrupting adopt (verifier W-021e)

brief said protection needs a strike 'beyond' the sold strike (false for a bull call spread) and futures protect 'only if the spec defines it' (REQ-059's covered-call example already does); round 1 then shipped a covered call that sent the short call first (verifier W-022)

brief said REQ-060 AC-2 is 'every run compares all non-exited strategies' (recalled from the W-021 PR); REQ-060 AC-2 actually reads 'It detects: missing platform position, unexpected broker position, quantity/strike/side/expiry mismatch, external broker modification, and partially executed strategy'. Caught by the builder (class 1).

the brief ordered 'finalize refuses unless Kite candles cover the last minute for every instrument' without quoting ADR-067, which says 'a minute Kite has no candle for keeps the live bar'; check_brief passed it (no quote = nothing to check); the final Tier A review reproduced 3 ways a day stays provisional forever; corrected in round 3 (brief-W-067-r3.md quotes ADR-067)

the brief let PowerShell's `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` stand in for `set -e`, from memory; the Tier A reviewer measured on this PC's pwsh 7.5.2 that a failing native program does not stop the script (PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=False), so the hook allowed exactly the masked commit it exists to block (CRITICAL); corrected in round 2.

Four brief rules not checked against the source: (1) W-103 brief said an undeclared audit key is 'refused' - REQ-063 AC-5 and filter_payload DROP it (caught by the orchestrator before dispatch); (2) W-102 brief said show an exit's margin 'as given' (negative) - ADR-099 says a closing basket counts as 0 (caught by the Tier A review); (3) W-102/W-103 briefs put REQ-056+REQ-073 / REQ-063+REQ-073 on one card - trace_check refuses one card for two requirements sharing AC numbers (caught by the builders); (4) every brief said 'no regenerated files' - docs/api/openapi.json is checked by test_committed_openapi_matches_the_app (caught by CI on W-105 and W-102). check_brief.py verifies quotes only, not unquoted rules.

occurrences.where: chunk 1 review fix brief F2 (orchestrator-written, session 5db71e90): chunk1-review-fix-f2-limits.md
occurrences.evidence: The brief told the builder that, when Kite states no wait after a 429, the wait is 'the endpoint group's own per-second window'. Finding F-60 (spec/findings.md:889) already recorded Kite staff: 'There's a cooldown period of 10s that must be respected whenever you receive a 429', extended by any send inside it. The builder read F-60 and kept the 10 s cooldown (correct); the orchestrator's recommended reconciliation of REQ-118 AC-3/AC-4 had rested on the wrong fact and was re-decided as ADR-179. New shape: an EXTERNAL API fact (Kite) written from memory while the registry held the measured answer. Practice from now: every Kite/vendor behaviour in a brief cites its F-id or is marked 'unverified - measure or cite before building'.

The brief told the checker 'No open question was answered (Q264 still open)'. Q264 was already DECIDED (ADR-080) before chunk 2 (open-questions.md line 413 at cf30134e); the Opus checker caught it. Sixteenth occurrence: a claim about spec state written without grepping the spec first.

occurrences.where: row 22 builder brief brief-22.md (orchestrator-written, session f1b75d11)
occurrences.evidence: The brief defined the expected move from the IV of the strategy leg nearest the spot as an 'orchestrator, technical' decision; the spec had already decided it: spot x ATM IV x sqrt(calendar days to expiry / 365) (REQ-027, Q254) with ATM IV = mean of the CE and PE IVs at the strike nearest the parity forward (REQ-106 AC-1). The builder built it and the Opus check PASSED it (the checker checked the brief's decision, not the spec). Found by the orchestrator only when spec_similar ran before writing the decision into the spec. Same brief: 'Reference: none - searched expected move, default range' although the Sensibull study was never searched (it has screens 013/020: SD bands, SD table); the owner asked the same hour whether Sensibull is referred to for every new thing. Seventeenth occurrence; a decision labelled 'technical' is the new shape - the label let it skip the spec grep.

fix: Brief rule for the orchestrator: every product rule in a brief quotes the spec text (file:line) it rests on; a rule the spec does not state is labelled 'orchestrator default (ADR-045) — not from the spec' so builders and verifiers challenge it. Verifiers already recompute from the spec.

detection.note: scripts/orchestrator/check_brief.py (W-040) checks every quoted spec citation in a brief verbatim against the cited REQ AC / ADR / Q text, before dispatch. It cannot see a paraphrase without quotes, a rule with no citation (reported UNCITED, fails only with --strict), or a correct quote used to support a wrong conclusion. Measured earlier: all 5 first occurrences were caught by builders or verifiers before merge; 4 cost a round, 1 parked an item (W-004). 2026-10-10 (W-067 r2): a paraphrased rule with no quote again cost a round - 'guarded' holds only for quoted rules; the orchestrator now quotes the decision text for every product rule it writes into a fix brief. 2026-10-10 (#155 r1): a second unquoted claim in one night - this time about TOOL behaviour (PowerShell), which check_brief cannot see at all. Status set back to unguarded: check_brief guards quoted decision and requirement text only. Practice until a mechanism exists: a claim in a brief about how a tool, shell or library behaves is either measured in the session first (the command and its output cited in the brief) or marked 'unverified - the builder must measure it'. 2026-10-23: a Kite behaviour claim with no F-id cost a decision (ADR-179); check_brief cannot see unquoted vendor facts either.
